suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-9 adds this relationship only as a bounded clinical proposition. Fecal incontinence is a recognized long-term bowel-function complication after surgical treatment for colon cancer. Require established colon cancer within the colorectal-cancer identity, actual colectomy or other bowel resection, and separately documented fecal incontinence with compatible postoperative chronology. Do not infer fecal incontinence from colorectal-cancer diagnosis alone, and do not generalize this colon-cancer surgical source to nonsurgical disease or rectal-cancer treatment without separate evidence. Preserve pre-existing continence disorders, neurologic disease, pelvic-floor dysfunction, inflammatory bowel disease, obstetric injury, medications, and other anorectal causes. The cited literature supports only this constrained relationship and does not, by itself, establish an individual medical nexus.
